newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank sells dollar-indexed Treasury notes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank sells dollar-indexed Treasury notes.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank sold Tuesday dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D) for a total face value of 950 million reais that it had held in its portfolio, dealers said.

The Bank sold 450 million reais of NTN-D notes that come due on April 1, 1997 and pay an annual yield of 11.32 percent. The Bank also sold 500 million reais of NTN-D notes coming due February 1, 1998 paying an annual yield of 10.95 percent.
Both series of NTN-Ds have a 24-month maturities and were part of the Central Bank's portfolio.
Dealers said the sale was part of an ongoing effort by the Central Bank to offer hedge opportunities and calm dollar futures markets, which have been anxious over Brazil's worsening trade profile.
The government announced this morning a $1.787 billion trade deficit for December, taking the 1996 trade gap to a record $5.539 billion.
Forex markets are already talking about a January deficit of between $800 million and $1.0 billion.
